messages.content: I’m mostly through the Front Range bookings. Can we start the early-December admissions conference in the Phoenix area? It’s Sunday Dec. 8 evening welcome through Tuesday afternoon, and there’s an optional Wednesday committee breakfast I may get assigned to. The official hotel is closest but has no breakfast and adds a daily fee. I need a practical comparison before I hold anything.

Yes. Two decisions will drive the rest: whether to arrive Saturday evening or Sunday midday, and whether to keep Wednesday open until the committee breakfast is confirmed. What part of Phoenix is the meeting in, and what are the official block rate and nearby hotel rates you’re seeing?

It’s in Tempe near Mill Ave. Official block is $219 a night plus a $24 daily destination fee, no breakfast. Hyatt Place is $178 and says breakfast included, about 0.8 miles away. Hampton is $169 with breakfast, more like 1.3 miles. SpringHill is $184 with breakfast but closer to 2 miles. Reception is 6:30 Sunday, Tuesday sessions end at 3:00, and the maybe-Wednesday breakfast would be 7:30 to 9:00.

First cut: the official block is the least stressful for walking and meeting access, but the fee and breakfast gap make it expensive. Hyatt Place looks like the strongest practical hold if its breakfast and cancellation terms check out: close enough for daylight walking, easy rideshare after evening events, and still likely cheaper than the official hotel. Hampton saves a little more but adds morning and evening friction. SpringHill only makes sense if it has a useful shuttle or a much better cancellation policy.
The destination fee is what worries me. Our reimbursement policy gets picky about resort or destination fees unless there really isn’t another workable option.

Then I would not make the official block your only safety net. For three nights, the official room is $657 plus $72 in fees before tax. Hyatt is $534 before tax; even a few short rideshares likely keep it comparable or cheaper, and breakfast is simpler. If the official block can be held with no penalty, it’s a backup. Otherwise, I’d focus on a refundable Hyatt hold.
That matches my instincts. For flights, I could arrive Saturday after dinner or Sunday midday. I’d rather not burn an extra night unless Sunday makes the reception risky.

With SLC to PHX nonstops, Sunday can work if you land by early afternoon. Saturday evening buys operational cushion and a calm Sunday morning, but it adds a hotel night and dinner logistics. Sunday midday is fine for a 6:30 reception if the flight arrives by about 1:30, but it becomes risky if the agenda adds any Sunday prep before late afternoon.
No Sunday prep on the draft agenda. Just registration by 5:30 and the reception at 6:30. Can you outline realistic flight windows, not exact booking yet?

I’d check these windows: Saturday Dec. 7 nonstop departing SLC around 6:00 to 7:30 p.m. if you want maximum cushion; Sunday Dec. 8 nonstop departing late morning and landing around 12:15 to 1:30 as the best balance; avoid Sunday arrivals after 3:00. For the return, if Wednesday breakfast becomes required, look for a Wednesday Dec. 11 nonstop around 1:30 to 3:30 p.m. If the breakfast is dropped, Tuesday evening could work after the dean’s dinner only if that dinner ends early enough.
I need to stay through Tuesday night either way; there’s a dean’s dinner Tuesday. Wednesday afternoon sounds safer. Is a rental car overkill?

For a Tempe-only conference, yes, a rental is probably overkill. PHX to Tempe is usually a short rideshare, and hotel parking plus conference traffic would eat into any savings. I’d plan rideshare airport-hotel-airport, then walk in daylight or use short rideshares for evening events.
I don’t mind a walk in daylight, but I don’t want a long walk alone after the reception.

That points back to Hyatt over Hampton. It is close enough for a daylight walk if the route feels comfortable, and short enough that an evening rideshare is not a big budget item. Ask whether the hotel shuttle covers the conference center or only the airport/local radius. If there is no shuttle, it’s still workable; just save rideshare receipts.
What do I need to document for reimbursement if I don’t use the official block?

Save a screenshot of the official block showing the $219 rate and $24 daily fee, your alternate hotel confirmation, and a brief note that the alternate is lower cost and includes breakfast. Make sure the hotel folio itemizes room and tax clearly. Keep rideshare receipts with origin and destination. If Wednesday breakfast becomes required, attach the agenda so Tuesday night and a Wednesday return are easy to justify.
Can you rank the hotel choices for a hold tonight?

Ranked for a refundable hold: 1) Hyatt Place in the Tempe/Mill Ave area, assuming breakfast and cancellation terms are confirmed. 2) Official block only as a backup if the fee is reimbursable or the meetings move into that hotel. 3) Hampton if Hyatt sells out; cheaper but farther after dark. 4) SpringHill only if the rate drops or it has a reliable shuttle. I’d hold Sunday-Wednesday for now, not Saturday, unless the Sunday agenda changes.
Please give me the quick call checklist so I can confirm before I hold Hyatt.

Call Hyatt and verify: cancellation deadline, breakfast start time Monday through Wednesday, late check-in, early bag drop if you arrive before the room is ready, shuttle radius or rideshare pickup spot, nearby dinner after the Sunday reception, any amenity or parking fees, and whether the final folio itemizes room and tax. Flight planning for now: target a Sunday nonstop landing by 1:30 p.m. and a Wednesday early-to-midafternoon nonstop until the committee breakfast is settled.

messages.content: The Phoenix agenda changed. Panel prep moved to Sunday at 4:00, and the Wednesday committee breakfast is now required. The Hyatt cancellable hold expires at 6 tonight. Official block is now only higher-rate rooms, $259 plus the same daily fee. I need to decide arrival day, hotel, and Wednesday return.
The Sunday panel prep makes arrival reliability the pressure point. What Sunday nonstop times are available from SLC, and is Saturday evening still possible if Sunday looks too tight?

Saturday is possible but annoying. Sunday I see Delta 10:20 a.m. to 12:05 p.m., Southwest 11:15 to 1:00, and then later flights. Return Wednesday has Delta 2:35 to 4:14 or Southwest 7:20 to 9:05. Hyatt is still $178 with breakfast and cancellable through Dec. 6.

Use Sunday only if you take the 10:20 to 12:05 nonstop. That gives you room for a rideshare, bag drop or check-in, and a reset before 4:00. The 11:15 to 1:00 is possible but thinner; anything later is not worth the risk. My pick: Sunday 10:20 outbound, Hyatt hold, and the 2:35 Wednesday return.
Would you still pick Hyatt now that Wednesday breakfast is required?

Yes, unless the Wednesday breakfast has moved inside the official hotel and starts unusually early. The rate gap is now bigger: official is $777 plus $72 in fees before tax for three nights, versus $534 before tax at Hyatt. You’ll need a few short rideshares, but Hyatt still wins on cost, breakfast access, and avoiding that destination fee.
Breakfast at Hyatt starts at 6:30 per the hotel page. The required committee breakfast is in the conference center 7:30 to 9:00 Wednesday. Does the 2:35 return leave too much dead time?

A little, but it’s useful slack rather than wasted time. Breakfast ends at 9:00, conversation may run to 9:30, then you can retrieve your bag and either work from the hotel lobby or head to PHX. A 2:35 flight lets you arrive at the airport around noon without rushing. The 7:20 return is only attractive if the office insists on the cheaper fare; otherwise it strands you most of the day.
Our office will pay a reasonable nonstop if the schedule makes sense. I just need clean documentation.

For the file, keep the agenda showing Sunday 4:00 panel prep and Wednesday required breakfast, the official block screenshot with the higher rate and destination fee, the Hyatt confirmation showing breakfast and cancellation terms, and rideshare receipts. For the flight, note that the afternoon return follows a required morning meeting and avoids an unnecessary late-evening airport wait.
Okay. Go with Sunday morning, Hyatt, Wednesday afternoon. Can you give me exact booking notes? Window if the seat maps are open.

Book SLC-PHX Sunday Dec. 8 on the 10:20 a.m. to 12:05 p.m. nonstop if the fare is still reasonable. Book PHX-SLC Wednesday Dec. 11 on the 2:35 to 4:14 p.m. nonstop. Choose Main Cabin or the equivalent rather than basic if you need easier changes and cleaner receipts. Select a window seat if available; if seat selection is deferred, set a check-in reminder.
And the hotel details to verify before I let the Hyatt hold become final?

Confirm Hyatt for Sunday Dec. 8 through Wednesday Dec. 11, cancellable through Dec. 6, breakfast at 6:30, late check-in, bag hold before check-in and after checkout, itemized folio with room and tax separated, any amenity or parking fees even without a car, and nearby dinner options after the Sunday reception. If those check out, let the Hyatt hold stand and skip the official block unless the conference moves key events into that hotel.

messages.content: Quick Phoenix update: the Wednesday committee breakfast moved to a university relations building farther east of campus, not the original conference center. My return flight also shifted 35 minutes earlier to 2:00. I need a tighter plan for checkout, luggage, and the airport.

What time does the breakfast end now, and will that building allow luggage in the room? If they won’t store bags, I’d avoid dragging a roller bag there unless the hotel stop truly breaks the airport buffer.
Breakfast is 7:45 to 9:15. The invite says space is tight and there’s no luggage storage. Hyatt confirmed they can hold my bag, checkout is 11, and hotel breakfast starts at 6:30.

Leave the bag at Hyatt. The extra hotel stop is cleaner than bringing luggage to a no-storage breakfast, and the 2:00 flight still leaves enough room. Start with coffee or a quick bite at 6:30, checkout and tag the bag around 7:00, request rideshare at 7:10, and aim to arrive by 7:30.
After breakfast, should I go straight back to the hotel or work near the committee building for a while?

Go back to Hyatt right after breakfast. If it ends at 9:15, request a ride around 9:25 and you should be back around 9:45. That gives you a stable place to retrieve the bag later and work from the lobby instead of juggling a carry-on in an unfamiliar building.
What’s the latest I should leave for PHX with the shifted flight?

For a 2:00 domestic departure, aim to be at PHX by noon. Request rideshare from Hyatt around 11:20 to 11:30; in normal traffic that should get you there around 11:45 to 11:55. If the breakfast runs long or security alerts look bad, leave the hotel closer to 11:10.
So hotel breakfast is optional since the committee breakfast includes food?

Yes. Treat hotel breakfast as coffee, water, and backup snack, not a full meal stop. Final Wednesday plan: checkout 7:00, leave luggage tagged at the Hyatt desk, rideshare 7:10, committee breakfast 7:45 to 9:15, return to Hyatt by about 9:45, work in the lobby, leave for PHX no later than 11:30, and keep the airline schedule-change email with your receipts.
